firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:238:| 2026-06-08 | **Fretboard link moves USB CDC host → direct FLEXCOM2 USART** (`actuator/fretboard_link.c`). The SAM9X75 Curiosity *Hybrid* board (new target, MCC ported in `598d370`/`3af09bc`) has no host-capable USB port, so the EDBG-CDC-bridge transport is gone. marvin now talks UART directly to the fretboard's SERCOM1: `PA13` FLEXCOM2_IO0 (TX) / `PA14` FLEXCOM2_IO1 (RX) ↔ fretboard `PB01` RX / `PB00` TX, 500 000 Bd 8N1. FLEXCOM2 regenerated in **ring-buffer mode** (RX ring 512 B, TX ring 64 B). The public `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` API and all perf-log records (FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE stamps, ACTUATOR, FRETBOARD_RAW) are unchanged, so `timing_pipeline`/`manual_control` and host `marvin-perf` need no edits. | The link is unchanged at the fretboard end (always SERCOM1 UART @ 500 000); only marvin's side was USB-bridged. Ring-buffer mode chosen over the basic single-transfer plib because the fretboard streams 17-byte frames continuously at 240 Hz: the basic plib disables RXRDY between a completed Read and the next arm, risking overrun, whereas the ring fills from its own ISR with no gap. RX is now a simple drain — a persistent read-threshold (`DS_FRAME_LEN`) notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which pulls bytes off the ring and runs the same `0x03 … 0xFC` resync as before; the separate `s_rx_stream` stream buffer + ISR re-arm are deleted (the ring *is* the buffer). TX drops the USB Write/ack-semaphore dance: a ring-buffer `Write` copies the byte and returns, so "ack" is the enqueue instant. No enumeration/attach/detach → `s_connected` becomes a static `s_link_up`. The `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` perf-stage name is now historical (it's a UART enqueue) but kept to avoid a host-decoder schema change. |

firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:244:| 2026-05-29 | Patch the UDPHS device driver to arm DMA for queued IRPs in completion ISRs. New helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` called after queue advance in `Tasks_ISR_DMA` and the ZLP-completion path. Logged as patch #9. | Stock Harmony USB v3.16.0 driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch — IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in the linked list but never get armed for transmission. Without this, `queueSizeWrite > 1` accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch — we'd accept three perf-log strips, transmit one, the other two stranded forever. The IRP-queue infrastructure is *already there* in the driver, the missing piece is the post-completion arm. Fix is additive (new helper, two new call sites, no refactor of existing IRPSubmit body), making it easy to find/maintain after MCC regen. Future Harmony versions may obviate this if upstream wires it up. |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:246:| 2026-05-29 | Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF) replaces CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE in the framing layer. `crc_*` field names renamed to `fcs_*` end-to-end. | USB hardware already CRCs every bulk packet on the wire; our framing-layer checksum's job is *firmware-side framing-bug detection* and *resync alignment* (false SOF in the middle of a corrupt stream). Fletcher-16 catches single-byte changes, adjacent swaps, and most non-adjacent swaps with ~1/65536 false-positive rate against random byte streams — sufficient for that job at ~2 cycles/byte (vs ~25 cycles for the bit-by-bit CRC, ~6 cycles for table-driven). SAM9X75 has no CRCCU peripheral (verified against `packs/SAM9X75D2G_DFP/component/`), so DMA-driven CRC isn't available. Wire format unchanged (still SOF+LEN+payload+16-bit checksum). One-shot wire-format break — old `.bin` captures aren't readable with new code; fine for dev. |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:247:| 2026-05-29 | Single `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES = 65000u` constant; `PERF_STRIP_MAX_W`/`MAX_H` removed. | The W×H pair was arbitrary — producer code only ever checks total bytes (`w * h * BPP <= PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`). Real binding constraint is the wire LEN field, which is `uint16_t` → max 65535 byte payload → max ~65 KB pixel per strip. Tighter than the UDPHS DMA cap (128 KB at `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE = 2`). Picking 65000 lands just under the LEN cap with margin. Producer accepts any (w, h) shape under that — practical envelope at 60 fps: 720×30, 480×45, 320×64, 290×72. Going beyond requires bumping LEN to u32, which is a wire-format break and not worth doing casually since wire bandwidth caps out around the same point at 60 fps. |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:249:| 2026-05-21 | `configMAX_PRIORITIES` bumped 5 → 8; tasks re-tiered into 4 active bands (UI=2, diagnostic+perf-wire=3, vision=4, strum-critical+host-wire=5) plus 3 reserve bands (1, 6, 7) and idle (0). MCC tasks re-prioritised via the per-component yml files so future regens preserve the layout. | Pre-change layout had 11 tasks bunched at priority 1 (9 MCC pollers + VideoTask + DetectorDrain) and 4 at priority 2, with no headroom. Two concrete problems: (a) VideoTask was *below* its consumer CvMarvinV1, a classic priority inversion that would bite during any priority-2 busy spell; (b) Legato (UI rendering) at the same priority as USB host driver tasks meant a heavy frame redraw could stall fretboard wire transit. The new layout puts strum-critical output above vision-real-time above diagnostic-I/O above UI, which matches the failure-cost ordering: a late strum is a missed note, a late detector tick recovers next frame, a late UI paint is jitter only. Reserve bands cost ~60 B BSS each, leave room for future watchdog or fault-recovery work to land without re-shuffling. Setting priorities in MCC yml (rather than patching `tasks.c` post-regen) avoids a re-apply patch — the source of truth and the emitted code now agree. |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:254:| 2026-05-20 | Relax Microchip's host CDC-ACM Communications-interface protocol check to accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0x00 (None)` in addition to `0x01 (AT_V250)` | The fretboard hardware exposes its UART to marvin via the on-board EDBG debugger's CDC ACM (composite VID=0x03EB PID=0x2175: HID + CDC ACM IAD + vendor + MSC). EDBG declares the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol=0x00` rather than the AT-command protocol Microchip hardcodes. The TPL/IAD match accepts the device (host stack does call `interfaceAssign`), but the per-interface check inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` then rejects the comm interface, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to STATE_ERROR, and our attach handler never fires. Both are CDC ACM in practice and Linux/macOS accept either. Two-line OR per check in `usb_host_cdc.c`; logged as patch #7 in the re-apply list. |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:255:| 2026-05-20 | `USB_HOST_Initialize` ordering relative to `DRV_USB_EHCI/OHCI_Initialize` and `Legato_Initialize` is **not** load-bearing — keep MCC's emitted order | A prior session hand-edited `initialization.c` to move `USB_HOST_Initialize` *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits on the theory that the host layer needed the HCD interfaces present at init time. Empirical retest with the CDC diagnostic logging in place: MCC's original order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well. The host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time, not at `USB_HOST_Initialize`. Reverted the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. (This is unrelated to patch #6, which is the *peripheral* init order — MMU/AIC ahead of TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC — that one is still a real regression and stays in the list.) |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:260:| 2026-05-20 | Reference-data export = SD card, format = detector-state + sparse keyframes | SD chosen over Ethernet/USB CDC because primary consumers are Edge-AI training (offline) and replay/sanity-check (offline). firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:291:| 2026-05-20 | cv_marvin_v1 sensor coords are in native capture-frame space, no 1920×1080 reference scaling | fret-tuner detect_video.py carries a 1920×1080 reference frame and scales coords at runtime — that frame size is what the Elgato HDMI-to-USB bridge produced, not a per-camera variable. The Wii is the primary production source at 480p60 = 720×480, so the static defaults are scaled from Python's 1920×1080 values by (3/8, 4/9) once at port time and stored in 720×480 space. firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:293:| 2026-05-20 | M2 fretboard link split into three layers — `detector → timing_pipeline → fretboard_link` — with the timing FIFO living on marvin and a 1-byte bitmask wire format | (a) Three-layer split keeps each concern small: detector emits state, timing_pipeline owns chord-window + strum scheduling, fretboard_link owns the USB CDC byte channel. Each can be replaced independently (different detector, different actuator transport) without touching the others. (b) Timing FIFO on marvin, not fretboard: marvin already runs the canonical detector and the recording pipeline, so co-locating timing keeps a single source of truth and avoids re-deriving state on the actuator side. Spec §4.4. The fretboard-takeover fallback (spec §6) is a separate mode where marvin disables its pipeline and fretboard runs `fret_button.c` standalone — that's the high-availability path, not the steady-state. (c) 1-byte bitmask matches `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py` and `firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h` exactly (G/R/Y/B/O at bits 0..4, strum-down bit 5, strum-up bit 6) — no reason to invent a new framing while the protocol is this small. Latest-wins semantics on the marvin→fretboard queue (depth 1 + overwrite) so a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale chords. (d) **Actuator-latency compensation deferred until mechanical actuators arrive.** Today's actuator is direct GPIO assertion on the fretboard PCB — latency ≈ 0, so today's design is sound. Future paths considered: (1) marvin compensates by subtracting a fretboard-published latency from `assert_at`/`strum_at`; (2) fretboard compensates by accepting timestamped events and scheduling locally. Path 2 needs a richer wire format (event + abs-timestamp); path 1 keeps the byte protocol but pushes the timing math up. Pick when we know which actuator (voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid) we're driving. |
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:325:- **MCC-file modifications maintenance risk.** A from-scratch MCC regen on 2026-05-15 confirmed **four** local modifications get clobbered. The 2026-05-20 USB-host regen added a fifth. Re-apply after every regen:
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:335:  5. **`initialization.c` `SYS_Initialize` — peripheral init order.** **(Hybrid board: the peripheral is now `FLEXCOM8_TWI_Initialize` (not FLEXCOM6) and there's no USB-host regen, but the MMU/AIC-before-peripherals concern still stands — verified intact on 2026-06-08: MMU/AIC run before TC0/FLEXCOM2/FLEXCOM8/XLCDC.)** The USB-host MCC regen (2026-05-20) reordered SYS_Initialize so that `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize` run *before* `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize`. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:346:  7. **`drv_usb_udphs_device.c` — multi-IRP DMA arming in completion ISRs.** Stock UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch (line 1604+); IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in (line 2273-2284 of patched file via `iterator->next = irp_t`) but never get armed for transmission. `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after firing the callback but does not re-program DMA hardware. Result: only one IRP per "queue idle" sequence ever transmits — the rest sit `STATUS_PENDING` forever.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:348:      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). Then add a call after the queue advance in **two** places:
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:355:      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:357:  8. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. Re-apply after every maXTouch MCC regen.

Bands are written straight to the sink (bypassing the small strip pool) and paced by the wire; emit is not gated by the STRIP type mask. `marvin-perf snapshot` reassembles and saves the frame (`.bgr` + sidecar `.json`, plus `.png` via Pillow). 88	/* Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF). USB hardware already CRCs every
89	 * bulk packet on the wire, so this checksum's job is *framing-layer*
90	 * detection only — false SOF matches during resync, firmware bugs that
91	 * write a wrong LEN or a partial frame. Fletcher catches single-byte
92	 * changes, adjacent swaps, and most non-adjacent swaps with ~1/65536
93	 * accidental-match rate against random byte streams — plenty for that
94	 * job, at ~2 cycles/byte vs ~6 for a table-driven CRC-16. Block-mod
95	 * pattern from RFC 1146 / Wikipedia: defer the modulo until uint32
96	 * could overflow, which gives ~5800 iterations between reductions. */
97	static uint16_t fletcher16(uint16_t init, const uint8_t *p, uint16_t len)
98	{
99	    uint32_t s1 = (uint32_t)(init & 0xFFu);
100	    uint32_t s2 = (uint32_t)((init >> 8) & 0xFFu);
101	
102	    while (len > 0u)
103	    {
104	        uint16_t blk = (len > 5802u) ? 5802u : len;
105	        len = (uint16_t)(len - blk);
106	        do
107	        {
108	            s1 += *p++;
109	            s2 += s1;
110	            blk--;
111	        } while (blk > 0u);
112	        s1 %= 255u;
113	        s2 %= 255u;
114	    }
115	
116	    return (uint16_t)((s2 << 8) | s1);
117	}

static void perf_log_drain_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize();
    register_post_scheduler_tasks();
    s_running = true;

    TickType_t last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
    bool prev_connected = false;

    for (;;)
    {
        bool now_connected = PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected();
        if (now_connected && !prev_connected)
        {
            emit_session_record();
        }
        prev_connected = now_connected;

        if (s_snapshot_req)
        {
            s_snapshot_req = false;
            emit_snapshot();
        }

        perf_rec_state_slot_t srec;
        if (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec,
                          pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
        {
            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
            /* Drain all currently queued state records before moving on.
             * Strips cost ~5 ms apiece on the wire, so a one-state-per-
             * iteration loop runs at ~50 Hz under load — well below the
             * ~700 stamps/s production rate. Same shape as the strip
             * drain below. */
            while (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec, 0) == pdTRUE)
            {
                PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
            }
        }

        /* Strip drain: dequeue slot index, write the slot's data via
         * pointer (no copy), return slot to the free pool. */
        uint8_t slot_idx;
        while (xQueueReceive(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) == pdTRUE)
        {
            const perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(r, strip_record_size(r));
            (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
        }

        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_drop) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS))
        {
            last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
            emit_drop_record();
            sample_and_emit_hwms();
            sample_and_emit_runtimes();
        }
    }
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-22 22:38:55Z)**_

I've pinned down enough to reframe this correctly. Two concrete findings first, then where I think the problem actually is.

## What the console output is actually telling you

1. **The banner you're seeing is the *normal, expected* end of the `bkptnone` variant.** You're running `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_bkptnone_defconfig` — that's the INIT_AND_STOP config. It initializes clocks/DDR and then deliberately halts with exactly that message ("Can load application via JTAG and jump") **every** boot, USB or not. That line is not itself the stall.

2. **marvin's own logs go to the *same* DBGU port.** `printf`/`LOG_*` are redirected through [xc32_monitor.c:69](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/stdio/xc32_monitor.c#L69) → `DBGU_Write`, i.e. the same FT4232H console channel showing the bootstrap banner. So when it works, after you JTAG-load-and-jump you'd expect marvin's boot logs (`PERF: USB device opened...`, video/TC358743 init, etc.) to appear on that same terminal.

**Therefore the real symptom is:** with USB connected, after the banner you get marvin's logs; with USB connected... you get *nothing more* — marvin either never gets loaded-and-jumped, or it hangs **before its first `printf`**. That's a hard, very-early stall, not a USB-enumeration problem.

## Why I don't think it's the firmware USB path

The obvious suspect would be the USB-device init, but it doesn't fit a pre-first-print hard hang:
- `USB_DEVICE_Initialize` / `DRV_USB_UDPHS_Initialize` in [initialization.c:504-508](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/initialization.c#L504) are Harmony non-blocking inits (real work deferred to `USB_DEVICE_Tasks`).
- The sink's open-retry loop and the cold-boot detach→attach workaround ([perf_log_sink_cdc.c:252-273](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L252)) run in a FreeRTOS task, *after* the scheduler and well after the first console logs. A wedge there wouldn't suppress marvin's early output.

## My leading hypothesis: VBUS back-powering → marginal power-on reset

This is a custom board (cHybrid REV1), and the symptom timing is the classic signature of USB VBUS bleeding through the UDPHS transceiver's ESD/clamp diodes into the 3.3 V rail:
- **Cable in before power-on** → rail is partially pre-charged → the SoC never sees a clean 0→3.3 V POR edge → DDR/PLL bring-up in bootstrap is marginal → marvin (loaded into DDR) runs on corrupt memory and hangs before printing. Banner still prints because that path is simpler/earlier.
- **Cable in after full boot** → rail already solidly up, no marginal POR → everything's fine.

That precisely matches "stalls if connected at boot, fine if connected after." A brownout from enumeration inrush during boot is a secondary variant of the same story.

## The one decisive test

Boot with a **data-only USB cable** (VBUS/pin-1 lifted or taped) to the SAM9X75 device port. If it boots cleanly that way, it's VBUS back-power and the fix is a hardware VBUS-isolation load (series Schottky or a load switch) — or just a firmware/procedural rule to enumerate only after boot. Complementary check: power the board **off**, plug in USB, and measure the 3.3 V rail — any significant voltage there confirms back-feed.

To point the next step precisely, a couple of things I can't see from here:

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Load marvin into DDR over JTAG and run it, with no SD card. macOS/OpenOCD only.
# The dev iteration loop: repeatable with no power-cycle (edit, rebuild, re-run).
# See load-ram.cfg for the mechanism.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   * No bootable medium present: JP3/JP4 (NAND/QSPI CS) OUT and no bootable microSD
#     (else RomBOOT boots it before reset init catches the core).
#   * Nothing else holding the FT4232H (e.g. kill a running debug OpenOCD server).
#
# Usage:   ./load-ram.sh
# Env overrides:
#   BOOTSTRAP_ELF  at91bootstrap init-and-stop ELF
#                  (default: ../binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf)
#   MARVIN_ELF     marvin ELF (default: ../out/marvin/default.elf)
#   FTDI_SERIAL    target a specific board by its FT4232H serial
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"

BOOTSTRAP_ELF="${BOOTSTRAP_ELF:-$root/binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf}"
MARVIN_ELF="${MARVIN_ELF:-$root/out/marvin/default.elf}"
FTDI_SERIAL="${FTDI_SERIAL:-}"

# XC32 ships binutils that read these ARM ELFs (just need the entry points).
xc32bin="$(ls -d /Applications/microchip/xc32/*/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
READELF="${READELF:-${xc32bin:+$xc32bin/}xc32-readelf}"

[ -f "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" ] || { echo "missing bootstrap ELF: $BOOTSTRAP_ELF" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -f "$MARVIN_ELF" ]    || { echo "missing marvin ELF: $MARVIN_ELF (build marvin first)" >&2; exit 1; }

boot_entry="$("$READELF" -h "$BOOTSTRAP_ELF" | awk '/Entry point/{print $NF}')"
marvin_entry="$("$READELF" -h "$MARVIN_ELF" | awk '/Entry point/{print $NF}')"

echo "bootstrap : $BOOTSTRAP_ELF (entry $boot_entry)"
echo "marvin    : $MARVIN_ELF (entry $marvin_entry)"

# Common args (never empty). A specific board serial, if given, must precede the
# config file that reads FTDI_SERIAL.
common=(-f "$here/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg" -f "$here/load-ram.cfg")
[ -n "$FTDI_SERIAL" ] && common=(-c "set FTDI_SERIAL $FTDI_SERIAL" "${common[@]}")

# marvin_load_ram (load-ram.cfg): reset init -> run bootstrap to completion -> load
# + run marvin.
exec openocd "${common[@]}" -c "init" \
        -c "marvin_load_ram $BOOTSTRAP_ELF $boot_entry $MARVIN_ELF $marvin_entry" \
        -c "shutdown"

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-22 22:42:58Z)**_

Important correction to my earlier assumption: `load-ram.sh` does a **warm nSRST reset** (`reset_config srst_only`, 500 ms pulse), not a power cycle — and the board stays powered across your edit/run loop. So this is *not* power-on back-power. The banner printing in the stalled case means `reset init` + bootstrap completed fine; the hang is **after `resume $marvin_entry`** — marvin runs but dies before its first `DBGU` print, and only when a USB host is actively attached to UDPHS at that moment. Let me find marvin's earliest print and any synchronous USB touchpoint before it.

So marvin's **first `LOG_*` is inside `APP_Initialize` → `log_init`** ([app.c:117-125](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c#L117)), which runs **during `SYS_Initialize`, before the FreeRTOS scheduler starts and before IRQs are unmasked**. "Totally dead, zero marvin characters" therefore means the hang is **inside the `SYS_Initialize` peripheral chain, before that first print** — and since IRQs are masked there, it can't be a USB interrupt. That points at a **polled/blocking hardware access** in the USB init. Let me check the UDPHS init and USB clock enable for a spin-wait.

    This is the dynamic implementation of F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_Initialize
    client interface initialization function for USB device.
    Function checks the input handle validity and on success initializes the
    driver object. It also freezes the clock, disables all DMA and Endpoint
    interrupts. The endpoint objects are updated with respective pointers

  Remarks:
    See drv_usb_udphs.h for usage information.
 */

void F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_Initialize
(
    DRV_USB_UDPHS_OBJ * drvObj,
    SYS_MODULE_INDEX index
)

{
    udphs_registers_t * usbID;      /* USB instance pointer */
    uint32_t count;                  /* Loop Counter */
    uint32_t dmaIndex;

    M_DRV_USB_UDPHS_InitUTMI();    
    
    /* Get the USB H/W instance pointer */
    usbID = drvObj->usbID;

    if(drvObj->operationSpeed == USB_SPEED_FULL)
    {
        /* Force Full-Speed */
        usbID->UDPHS_TST = UDPHS_TST_SPEED_CFG_FULL_SPEED;
    }
    else
    {
        /* Default - High Speed */
        usbID->UDPHS_TST &= UDPHS_TST_SPEED_CFG_NORMAL;
    }

    usbID->UDPHS_CTRL = UDPHS_CTRL_EN_UDPHS_Msk;
 
    /* Point the objects for control endpoint. It is a bidirectional
     * endpoint, so only one object is needed */
    drvObj->deviceEndpointObj[0] = &gDrvUSBControlEndpoints[index][0];

    /* DMA endpoint capable */
    gDrvUsbUdphsDeviceEndpointFeatureDescription  = DRV_USB_UDPHS_EPT_DMA;
    /* 3 banks endpoints capable (<<16) */
    gDrvUsbUdphsDeviceEndpointFeatureDescription |= DRV_USB_UDPHS_EPT_BK;
    
    /* Point the objects for non control endpoints.
     * They are unidirectional endpoints, so multidimensional
     * array with one object per endpoint direction */

    for(count = 1; count < DRV_USB_UDPHS_ENDPOINTS_NUMBER ; count++)
    {
        drvObj->deviceEndpointObj[count] = &gDrvUSBNonControlEndpoints[index][count - 1U];
    }

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-22 22:49:52Z)**_

## Root cause found

The hang is a hardware-clock spin-wait, not a USB-stack problem. Here's the full chain:

**Where it hangs:** [plib_clk.c:88-92](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/clk/plib_clk.c#L88) —

```c
/* STEP 10: Wait for the lock bit to rise by polling the PMC_PLL_ISR0 */
while ((PMC_REGS->PMC_PLL_ISR0 & PMC_PLL_ISR0_LOCKU_Msk) != PMC_PLL_ISR0_LOCKU_Msk)
{ /* Wait */ }
```

This is an **unbounded wait for the UTMI PLL (UPLL) to lock** — and the UPLL *is* the USB 2.0 HS PHY's PLL. It's called from `initUPLLCLK()` → `CLK_Initialize()`, which is the **very first line of `SYS_Initialize`** ([initialization.c:428](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/initialization.c#L428)).

**Why every observable lines up:**
- It's the first thing marvin does, long before DBGU logging or the display → **totally dead, zero marvin characters** on the shared DBGU console. ✓ (I confirmed DBGU output is polled/synchronous at [plib_dbgu.c:217](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/dbgu/plib_dbgu.c#L217), so if marvin ran at all past this you'd see text.)
- IRQs are masked in `SYS_Initialize`, so it can't be a USB interrupt — it's a **polled analog-lock** on the one clock physically coupled to the port the host is plugged into. ✓
- The bootstrap banner still prints because at91bootstrap brings up PLLA/DDR/console but **not** the UPLL — marvin is the first code to enable it. ✓
- **Connect-after-boot works** because the UPLL locked cleanly during the earlier host-free `CLK_Initialize`; later attach never re-runs it. ✓

**Mechanism:** `load-ram.sh` does a *warm* `nSRST` reset (`reset_config srst_only`, [sam9x75-chybrid.cfg:25](firmware/marvin/openocd/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg#L25)), **not a power cycle** — the board stays powered across your edit/run loop. When a host is actively driving VBUS + D+/D− and the UTMI bandgap/regulator/PLL analog block ([plib_clk.c:68-89](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/clk/plib_clk.c#L68)) is brought up on a not-power-cycled PHY, the UPLL never reaches lock, so `initUPLLCLK` spins forever. (Note: the SAMA7 UTMI path resets the PHY via `RSTC_GRSTR.USB_RST` before the PLL — the SAM9X75 RSTC has **no** such bit, so there's no PHY-reset step here to clear a host-dirtied PHY.)

## Confirm it with one test

Power-cycle the board **cold** (full power off/on, not `reset init`) with the USB host attached the whole time, then load marvin:
- **Boots fine cold, hangs on warm reset** → confirms the warm-reset-dirty-PHY mechanism above; and importantly means production NAND/SD (cold-POR) boot is likely unaffected.
- **Hangs even cold with host attached** → it's VBUS/analog-level; a data-only cable (VBUS lifted, or D+/D− lifted) will tell you which line is the aggressor.

## Fixes

1. **Today, zero code (what you're already doing):** keep the UDPHS cable out during `load-ram.sh`; attach after marvin is up. Reliable because it guarantees a clean UPLL lock.
2. **Dev-loop ergonomics:** if you must leave USB attached, power-cycle instead of warm-reset before loading.
3. **Proper firmware guard** would be a timeout on that `LOCKU` spin — but [plib_clk.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/clk/plib_clk.c) is MCC-generated (the "don't edit vendor tree" rule), and nothing runs before `CLK_Initialize` to wrap it. So a robust firmware fix isn't clean here without touching generated code; that's a decision to make deliberately, not silently.

I'd recommend running the cold-vs-warm test first — it decides whether this is purely a JTAG-dev-loop annoyance (workaround #1 is the answer) or a real risk for production boot (then we design a sanctioned guard). Want me to record this root cause in [firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md) once you've run the cold/warm test?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-22 22:56:21Z)**_

That detail rules out the power/warm-reset mechanisms and, importantly, **exonerates marvin's USB device path**: `USB_DEVICE_Attach` and the VBUS read only happen after `App_StartServices`, which fires *after the splash is on screen* ([app.c:161-165](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c#L161)). Since your stall is a totally-dead display (no splash), the hang is **before that** — either the pre-scheduler `SYS_Initialize` clock/peripheral chain or the UI boot task before its first render. PC8 being a plain GPIO input can't gate that code, so the real correlating variable is most likely the **D+/D− lines** being connected to the host (which the cable connects regardless of VBUS), not the sense pin.

I've gone as far as static analysis usefully can. The decisive move — and it's cheap since you're already on JTAG — is to **halt the stalled core and read PC/backtrace**. That converts all of this into a single fact.

## Read the PC at the stall (definitive)

`load-ram.sh` ends with `shutdown`, so after it stalls, attach a *fresh* OpenOCD that **only inits + halts** (no reset, or you'll restart it):

```bash
cd firmware/marvin
# Terminal 1: attach WITHOUT resetting the running (stalled) core
openocd -f openocd/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg -c "init" -c "halt" \
        -c "reg pc" -c "reg sp" -c "resume" -c "shutdown"
```

For a symbolized backtrace (more useful), leave the server up and use gdb against the ELF you loaded:

```bash
# Terminal 1:
openocd -f openocd/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg -c "init"
# Terminal 2:
xc32-gdb out/marvin/default.elf \
  -ex "target extended-remote :3333" -ex "monitor halt" \
  -ex "bt" -ex "info registers" -ex "detach" -ex "quit"
```

- If PC/backtrace lands in **`initUPLLCLK` / `CLK_Initialize`** ([plib_clk.c:89](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/clk/plib_clk.c#L89)) → confirmed it's the UTMI PLL not locking with the host on D+/D−.
- If it's somewhere else (a driver init, Legato, a UI boot-task loop) → we chase that instead. Either way, no more guessing.

## Cheap A/B test to isolate VBUS_SENSE vs. data lines

Run twice with a modified cable to the UDPHS port:
1. **Pin-1 (VBUS) taped**, D+/D− intact → PC8 reads low, host still on data lines. Boots? → PC8/VBUS_SENSE is somehow the trigger. Still hangs? → it's the data lines.
2. **D+/D− (pins 2&3) taped**, VBUS intact → the inverse.

Combined with the PC read, that fully pins the mechanism. Paste the backtrace and I'll take it from there — and once we know the true cause I'll write it up in [the journal](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md).

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-22 23:45:01Z)**_

Resolved to line 2726 — the **entry** of the UDPHS ISR. A single-sample halt landing right at the ISR entry is the classic signature of an **interrupt storm**: the handler runs, returns, and immediately re-fires. And look at the entry logic — [drv_usb_udphs_device.c:2726-2735](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c#L2726): if `hDriver->isOpened == false` (or no callback yet), the ISR **logs and returns without clearing any interrupt flag**. So if the UDPHS interrupt is enabled at the AIC while a host is asserting a condition, but the driver hasn't been *opened* yet, the flag never clears → the CPU is pinned in the ISR forever → tasks never run → splash never renders → dead.

That fits everything: marvin opens/attaches the device late (in the perf drain task, post-splash, [perf_log_sink_cdc.c:252-273](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L252)); attach-after-boot works because by then it's opened and clears interrupts. The crux for a fix is **where the UDPHS AIC source gets enabled relative to the open**. Let me check.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-22 23:48:47Z)**_

Confirmed — full root cause, code-verified end to end.

## Root cause: UDPHS interrupt storm during boot

1. `AIC_INT_Initialize()` (in `SYS_Initialize`, [initialization.c:439](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/initialization.c#L439)) **unconditionally enables the UDPHS interrupt at the AIC** — [plib_aic.c:126](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/aic/plib_aic.c#L126) writes `AIC_IECR` for every table entry, and UDPHS is entry 23, **level-sensitive** ([plib_aic.c:78](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/aic/plib_aic.c#L78)).
2. Marvin doesn't **open** the USB device until the perf-drain task runs `PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize()` — which is spawned by `App_StartServices`, *after* the splash is on screen ([app.c:161-165](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c#L161)).
3. When the scheduler starts and unmasks IRQs, if a host is attached the UDPHS asserts an interrupt (bus reset / EP0 activity). The ISR runs, hits [drv_usb_udphs_device.c:2726](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c#L2726), sees `isOpened == false`, and **returns without clearing anything**. Because the AIC source is level-sensitive, the line stays asserted → the ISR re-fires immediately → **100% CPU in the ISR** → no task ever advances → the UI boot task never renders the splash → dead display.

Your halt landed exactly at the ISR entry (`pc=0x23f085c8` → `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_Tasks_ISR`), the textbook storm signature. And it matches every observation: dead display, deterministic across cold power-cycles, and **fine when attached after boot** (by then the device is opened, so the ISR services and clears interrupts). It's the **D+/D− connection**, not VBUS/PC8 — PC8 is only read later in the driver's task state machine.

## Proposed fix

The bug is in MCC-generated code (the ISR early-returns without masking, and the AIC enables the source before the driver is opened) — which I won't edit per the project rule. The clean, self-contained fix lives entirely in **our** files: keep the UDPHS source masked at the AIC from boot until the sink has actually opened + attached the device.

- **[app.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c) `APP_Initialize`** (pre-scheduler): `SYS_INT_SourceDisable(UDPHS_IRQn);` — mask it before IRQs are ever unmasked, closing the window entirely (global IRQs are still off during `SYS_Initialize`, so masking here is race-free).
- **[perf_log_sink_cdc.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c) `PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize`** (after the `USB_DEVICE_Open` + `EventHandlerSet` + forced detach→attach at [lines 252-273](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L252)): `SYS_INT_SourceEnable(UDPHS_IRQn);` — unmask only once the driver can service and clear interrupts.

This makes boot-with-cable behave like attach-after-boot: enumeration just proceeds normally once the sink is live. `USB_DEVICE_Open` and the retry loop don't need the interrupt, so masking it in between is safe.

**Interim workaround (no code):** what you're already doing — leave the UDPHS cable out until marvin is up, then plug in.

Want me to implement the two-line mask/unmask fix and record the root cause + decision in [the journal](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md)? I'd build-check it, but I won't commit without your go-ahead.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-22 23:59:10Z)**_

Since init leaves the UDPHS with `IEN = 0`, all interrupts cleared, and the D+ pull-up **detached** ([drv_usb_udphs_device.c:177-216](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c#L177)), the storm can't come from the raw init state — some `IEN` bit has been set and a source is asserting by the time it wedges. There are two possible defect modes, and which one it is changes the exact patch. A ~2-minute register capture at the stall disambiguates it — and it's exactly the hard data a bug report needs.

## 1. Capture ground truth at the stall

With the board wedged, attach without resetting and read the UDPHS + driver state (register addresses from the DFP: base `0xf803c000`, `IEN`=`+0x10`, `INTSTA`=`+0x14`, `CTRL`=`+0x00`, `CLRINT`=`+0x18`):

```bash
cd firmware/marvin
# Terminal 1:
openocd -f openocd/sam9x75-chybrid.cfg -c "init"
# Terminal 2:
xc32-gdb out/marvin/default.elf -ex "target extended-remote :3333" -ex "monitor halt" \
  -ex "x/1xw 0xf803c010"  `#UDPHS_IEN` \
  -ex "x/1xw 0xf803c014"  `#UDPHS_INTSTA` \
  -ex "x/1xw 0xf803c000"  `#UDPHS_CTRL (DETACH bit shows attach state)` \
  -ex "p gDrvUSBUDPHSObj[0].isOpened" \
  -ex "p gDrvUSBUDPHSObj[0].pEventCallBack" \
  -ex "bt"
# Sample PC ~5x to confirm it's pinned in the ISR:
#   (monitor halt; monitor reg pc; monitor resume) repeated
```

Interpretation:
- **`isOpened == 0`** → the storm is the *no-client* path. Whatever is in `INTSTA & IEN` is asserting with no one to service it.
- **`isOpened == 1`, callback non-NULL** → the storm is an *enabled source the else-branch fails to clear*. `INTSTA & IEN` names it (likely `ENDRESET`, `WAKE_UP`, or `DET_SUSPD`).

## 2. The defect (vendor code)

Common to both modes: **`F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_Tasks_ISR` has return paths that don't guarantee the interrupt line is de-asserted before it exits.** On the SAM9x/SAMA5 **AIC**, the UDPHS source is configured `LEVEL_SENSITIVE` ([plib_aic.c:78](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/aic/plib_aic.c#L78)), so `SYS_INT_SourceStatusClear` (AIC ICCR, [drv_usb_udphs.c:534](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs.c#L534)) is a no-op while the peripheral keeps the line high — the ISR re-enters immediately and pins the CPU. This is masked on the NVIC-based families (edge/pulse latching hides the missing peripheral-ack), which is likely why it hasn't surfaced.

**Contributing factor:** `AIC_INT_Initialize` unconditionally enables *every* tabled source via `AIC_IECR` ([plib_aic.c:126](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/aic/plib_aic.c#L126)), including UDPHS, before the driver has a client — whereas the UDPHS driver's `Open`/`Attach` never call `SYS_INT_SourceEnable` (they assume the source is already live and only *disable* it around critical sections). So the driver's ISR must be robust to firing before/without a client.

## 3. Candidate fixes

**Mode A — no-client path** ([drv_usb_udphs_device.c:2726-2735](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c#L2726)). Today both no-client branches only `SYS_DEBUG_MESSAGE` and fall through. Acknowledge + mask so the line drops:

```c
if ((false == hDriver->isOpened) || (NULL == hDriver->pEventCallBack))
{
    /* No client can service this interrupt yet. On a level-sensitive
     * interrupt controller (SAM9x/SAMA5 AIC) simply returning re-enters
     * this ISR indefinitely. Mask all UDPHS sources and clear pending
     * status so the request de-asserts; IEN is re-programmed when a
     * client attaches / enables EP0. */
    usbID = hDriver->usbID;
    usbID->UDPHS_IEN   = 0U;
    usbID->UDPHS_CLRINT = UDPHS_CLRINT_Msk;
    SYS_DEBUG_MESSAGE(SYS_ERROR_INFO,
        "\r\nUSB UDPHS Driver: interrupt with no client; masking.");
}
else
{
    usbID = hDriver->usbID;
    /* ... existing handling ... */
}
```

**Mode B — unhandled enabled source in the else branch.** If e.g. `ENDRESET`/`WAKE_UP` is set in both `IEN` and `INTSTA` but the code path for that state doesn't write the matching `UDPHS_CLRINT` bit, add the missing `UDPHS_CLRINT = <that bit>` clear. The capture's `INTSTA & IEN` value points straight at the offending case block.

**Deeper/root fix (broader blast radius, worth flagging in the report):** have the UDPHS driver own its AIC source — `SYS_INT_SourceEnable` in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_Open` (or first `Attach`) and leave `AIC_INT_Initialize` from blanket-enabling sources whose drivers open later. This aligns SAM9/AIC behavior with the NVIC families and removes the pre-client window entirely.

I'd recommend submitting **Mode A** as the concrete robustness fix (it's correct regardless and low-risk), with the capture data attached and the AIC-enable-ordering noted as the underlying design gap.

## 4. For the report

- **Component:** Harmony USB device driver `drv_usb_udphs` (`F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_Tasks_ISR`), with a supporting note on the `csp` AIC PLIB (`AIC_INT_Initialize`). Confirm the exact driver version from your `harmony-manifest`/`.yml` — this tree corresponds to USB driver v3.16.0 per our journal.
- **Affected:** SAM9x60/SAM9X7x/SAMA5 (AIC, level-sensitive) in interrupt mode; not NVIC parts.
- **Repro:** USB device (CDC) with a host attached during boot, where the app opens/attaches the device sometime after `SYS_Initialize`. ISR storms → system hangs. Works if host is attached after the stack is fully up.
- **Expected/actual:** ISR must leave its interrupt de-asserted on every exit path; instead it returns with the AIC line still asserted → infinite re-entry.

Want me to run the capture commands' analysis with you once you have the `IEN`/`INTSTA`/`isOpened` values, and record the root cause + whichever fix mode it turns out to be in [the journal](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md)?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-23 00:07:12Z)**_

Decisive. Here's the decode of your capture:

| Register | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `UDPHS_IEN` (0x…010) | `0x00000010` | **bit 4 = ENDRESET** interrupt enabled |
| `UDPHS_INTSTA` (0x…014) | `0x0000003a` | bits 1,3,4,5 asserted (DET_SUSPD, INT_SOF, **ENDRESET**, WAKE_UP) |
| `UDPHS_CTRL` (0x…000) | `0x00000100` | EN_UDPHS set, **DETACH=0 → controller *attached*** (D+ pull-up on) |
| `isOpened` | `false` | **driver has no client** |
| `pEventCallBack` | `0x0` | **no event handler registered** |

`IEN & INTSTA = 0x10` → **ENDRESET is the enabled, asserted source**. The controller is *attached*, so the connected host keeps issuing bus resets → ENDRESET keeps latching. But the driver has no client, so the ISR takes the `isOpened==false` early-return at [drv_usb_udphs_device.c:2726](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c#L2726) and **never writes `UDPHS_CLRINT`**. The wrapper's `SYS_INT_SourceStatusClear` ([drv_usb_udphs.c:534](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs.c#L534)) only touches the AIC, which is **level-sensitive** — so the line stays high and the ISR re-enters forever. Your backtrace (`FreeRTOS_IRQ_Handler → DRV_USB_UDPHS_Handler → DRV_USB_UDPHS_Tasks_ISR`, pinned) is exactly that storm. **Confirmed Mode A.**

## Primary defect + fix (submit this)

**Defect:** `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_Tasks_ISR` has no-client return paths (`isOpened==false`, `pEventCallBack==NULL`) that return **without acknowledging the pending peripheral interrupt**. On a level-sensitive controller (SAM9x/SAMA5 AIC) this is an unrecoverable interrupt storm. (Latches on NVIC parts hide it, which is why it hasn't shown up there.)

**Fix** — de-assert before returning, at [drv_usb_udphs_device.c:2726-2735](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c#L2726):

```c
if ((false == hDriver->isOpened) || (NULL == hDriver->pEventCallBack))
{
    /* No client can service this interrupt. On a level-sensitive
     * interrupt controller (SAM9x/SAMA5 AIC) returning here without
     * acknowledging re-enters this ISR indefinitely. Mask all UDPHS
     * sources and clear pending status so the request de-asserts; the
     * stack re-programs UDPHS_IEN when a client opens and attaches. */
    usbID = hDriver->usbID;
    usbID->UDPHS_IEN    = 0U;
    usbID->UDPHS_CLRINT = UDPHS_CLRINT_Msk;
    SYS_DEBUG_MESSAGE(SYS_ERROR_INFO,
        "\r\nUSB UDPHS Driver: interrupt with no client; masking.");
}
else
{
    usbID = hDriver->usbID;
    /* ... existing handling unchanged ... */
}
```

(Note `usbID` is currently only assigned inside the `else`; the fix assigns it in the no-client branch too.) This self-heals: once a client opens + attaches, the normal reset/endpoint path re-enables `IEN`.

## Secondary finding worth including

How the controller reaches *attached + ENDRESET-enabled + no client* is itself a bug, and it's why this is 100% reproducible in your JTAG load-to-RAM loop:

- Your `CTRL = 0x100` is the exact footprint of `DRV_USB_UDPHS_Deinitialize` ([drv_usb_udphs.c:330](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs.c#L330)): `usbID->UDPHS_CTRL = UDPHS_CTRL_EN_UDPHS_Msk`. That write **clears DETACH — leaving the device *attached*** (deinit should *detach*), and it **never clears `UDPHS_IEN`** — so a de-initialized controller still presents a pull-up to the host and keeps bus interrupts armed with no client to service them.
- The `nSRST` warm reset (`reset init` in `load-ram.sh`) resets the core + AIC (so `AIC_INT_Initialize` re-enables the UDPHS AIC source) but **the UDPHS block retains `CTRL`/`IEN`/`INTSTA` across the warm reset**, while the freshly-loaded image's driver object is zeroed (`isOpened=false`). Host still connected → ENDRESET asserted → storm before a client exists. A cold POR should reset the block, so if cold boot also hangs it's the live open→attach→lose-client path — worth a second capture on a true cold boot to compare.

So there are really two things to flag: (1) the ISR must ack on every exit path (the fix above), and (2) `DRV_USB_UDPHS_Deinitialize` should **set DETACH and clear `UDPHS_IEN`** rather than leaving the port attached and armed.

## Report packaging

- **Component:** Harmony USB device driver `drv_usb_udphs` — `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_Tasks_ISR` (primary) and `DRV_USB_UDPHS_Deinitialize` (secondary). Confirm the driver version from your `harmony-manifest`/`.yml`; this tree is v3.16.0 per our journal.
- **Affected:** AIC-based parts (SAM9x60/SAM9X7x, SAMA5) in interrupt mode; NVIC parts mask the symptom.
- **Repro:** USB CDC device with a host attached during boot / across a warm (JTAG `reset init`) reload, before the app opens+attaches. ISR storms → total hang before the app runs.
- **Expected vs actual:** ISR must leave its interrupt de-asserted on every exit path; instead it returns with the AIC line still asserted (ENDRESET), re-entering indefinitely.
- **Evidence:** the register table above + the `FreeRTOS_IRQ_Handler → …_Tasks_ISR` backtrace.

Want me to record this confirmed root cause, the register evidence, and both fixes in [the journal](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md)? And if useful I can draft the workaround note (mask `UDPHS_IRQn` until the sink opens) as our local mitigation while the driver fix is in flight.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-23 00:25:58Z)**_

Confirmed in the binary — the no-client branch now does, in order:

```
ldr r3,[r5,#28]      ; r3 = hDriver->usbID
ldr r2,[r3]          ; CTRL
orr r2,r2,#0x200     ; |= DETACH        ← disconnect D+ pull-up
str r2,[r3]
str #0,[r3,#16]      ; UDPHS_IEN   = 0  ← mask sources
str #0xFE,[r3,#24]   ; UDPHS_CLRINT     ← clear pending (incl. ENDRESET)
pop {...pc}
```

So on the first no-client interrupt it detaches, and DETACH survives USB bus resets — the host sees the device disappear and stops hammering it, which ends the re-arm loop that defeated the mask-only version.

- Whether `marvin-perf` can enumerate afterward — that exercises the sink's forced detach→attach recovery ([perf_log_sink_cdc.c:271-273](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L271)).

- **`AIC_ISR = 0x17` = source 23 = UDPHS** is the interrupt in service; **`IPR0` bit 23 set** — UDPHS is the storming source, confirmed at the controller level (not inferred).
- **All 8 PC samples are in interrupt code** — `FreeRTOS_IRQ_Handler` ↔ `DRV_USB_UDPHS_Tasks_ISR` ↔ `AIC_INT_IrqDisable`, zero in task code. `xSchedulerRunning = 0`. So the scheduler **never starts** — the storm pins the CPU inside `SYS_Initialize`→scheduler-start, which is why "main.c:40" and dead display.
- **`CTRL = 0x100`** — the controller is **still attached** (DETACH bit 9 clear) despite my in-ISR detach, and **`IEN = 0x10`** (ENDRESET re-armed). My reactive detach loses the race: the host's next bus reset resets the UDPHS core, which re-clears DETACH and re-arms ENDRESET faster than the breaker can hold.

**Your "first load stalls, second load works" is the decisive clue.** On a POR-fresh boot the controller comes up **attached with ENDRESET armed before marvin's USB stack has a client** — the host immediately storms it with bus resets and the CPU never escapes to start the scheduler. On the second (warm) load the state differs (host has backed off / peripheral not POR-fresh), so no storm.

The reactive ISR approach can't win this race. The real bug is in **init**: `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_Initialize` leaves the controller *attached*. Look at [drv_usb_udphs_device.c:177-183](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c#L177) — it sets DETACH, then does "Reset IP" (`EN_UDPHS` 0→1) which **resets the core and clears the DETACH bit it just set**, so init finishes attached (`CTRL=0x100`, exactly what we see). Fix: detach *after* the reset.

## The decisive test

This one specifically targets your failing case — **cold power cycle, USB host attached, first load**:

```bash
# power-cycle the board, leave the UDPHS cable attached, then:
cd firmware/marvin && ./openocd/load-ram.sh
```

Expected now: the host sees nothing on the bus during bring-up (device detached), so no ENDRESET storm → scheduler starts → splash/LVDS comes up → post-splash the perf sink calls `USB_DEVICE_Attach`, the pull-up connects, and the host enumerates (`PERF: USB device opened…` → `…CDC configured`), `marvin-perf` connects.

If it boots on the **first** load with the cable attached, that's the fix — the init-detach removes the startup race entirely, which is why both loads should now behave like your "second load."

Quick confirmation if you want it: while running normally, `UDPHS_CTRL` (0xf803c000) should read with **bit 9 set (`0x2xx`/`0x[AB]xx`)** early in boot (detached), then clear once the sink attaches; and a halt should land in real task code, not `DRV_USB_UDPHS_Tasks_ISR`.

Two notes:
- I left the **ISR no-client breaker** (detach + mask) in place as defensive belt-and-suspenders. For the bug report, the **init-ordering fix is the root cause** (detach clobbered by the post-set EN reset), and the ISR fix is the robustness hardening — both are legitimate, independent defects.
- If enumeration doesn't come up cleanly *after* boot now (i.e., boot is fixed but `marvin-perf` won't connect), that's a separate, much friendlier problem in the attach/recovery path, not a hang.

Report back on the cold-first-load test.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-23 00:49:24Z)**_

Confirmed in the binary:
- **`SYS_Initialize`**: immediately after `bl AIC_INT_Initialize` → `mov r0,#23; bl SYS_INT_SourceDisable` — UDPHS (source 23) is masked at the AIC the instant after the AIC enables it, still early in `SYS_Initialize` with CPU IRQs masked, so there's **no window** for it to fire.
- **`PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize`**: `mov r0,#23; bl SYS_INT_SourceEnable` — re-enabled only after the sink has opened, registered its handler, and attached.

## Why this one should hold where the others didn't

The previous fixes all operated *inside* the UDPHS ISR or the controller — they could only react *after* an interrupt was already being delivered, and they kept losing the race to the host's bus-reset retries (which re-arm ENDRESET and re-attach across `nSRST`, hence the variable "N loads"). This fix removes the interrupt from the AIC delivery path entirely for the whole boot. A masked source **cannot** vector the CPU no matter what the controller or host do — so `SYS_Initialize` finishes, the scheduler starts, the UI comes up, and only when the perf sink is genuinely ready (device open + handler set + attached, post-splash) does UDPHS get enabled and enumerate.

## Test

The determinism is the whole point, so please hammer the previously-failing case:

```bash
# cold power-cycle, UDPHS cable attached, then:
cd firmware/marvin && ./openocd/load-ram.sh
```

- It should now boot on the **first** load, **every** time (try several power-cycles).
- After boot, confirm `marvin-perf` still enumerates/connects — that verifies the deferred `SYS_INT_SourceEnable` path re-arms USB correctly.

If it boots reliably: we've got it, and I'll write up the journal entry. The three earlier driver edits (ISR no-client detach+mask, and the init-detach ordering) are still legitimate independent defects worth keeping in the bug report, but **this AIC-masking is the operative fix** — and it reframes the root cause cleanly for Microchip: `AIC_INT_Initialize` blanket-enables every source (incl. UDPHS) before the owning driver has a client, so the UDPHS driver should gate its own AIC source on open/attach rather than assuming it's safe to be live from reset. Our mask-until-ready is that pattern applied at the app boundary.

If it *still* stalls after this, then the storm is being delivered by something other than the path I think, and I'll want a fresh `AIC_ISR`/`IPR0` capture — but a masked source storming would point at an AIC/silicon issue rather than the driver.

Run that and paste it. The decision tree from the results:

- **(1) `x/4i 0x23f2f3c0`** — should show `bl AIC_INT_Initialize` then `mov r0, #23; bl SYS_INT_SourceDisable`. If it *doesn't*, the running image is stale — load-ram isn't loading my build, and no source fix matters until that's sorted (rebuild path mismatch).
- **(3) AIC IMR for source 23** — after `SSR<-23`, IMR bit0 (the selected source's mask) tells us if UDPHS is enabled at the AIC *right now*. If it's **enabled** despite my init mask, the USB stack re-enabled it during boot (case 2) → the fix has to prevent that (keep it detached so no reset/EP0-enable path fires, or gate the stack), not just mask once.
- **(2) AIC_ISR / (4) IPR0** — confirms whether source 23 is still the one in-service/pending, or something else entirely.
- **(5) `CTRL`/`isOpened`/`status`** — `status` (READY = 3) tells us if `DEVICE_Initialize` even ran; `CTRL` bit 9 tells us attached vs detached now.

My leading bet is **case 2**: the device stack enables EP0 early (which calls `SYS_INT_SourceEnable(UDPHS_IRQn)`), re-arming the source I masked, and the controller is attached (persisted across `nSRST`, since `nSRST` doesn't reset UDPHS) so the host storms it. If (3) shows source 23 re-enabled, that's confirmed — and the fix shifts to keeping the **peripheral** from generating interrupts at all until ready (hold `EN_UDPHS`/pull-up off, or gate `ID_UDPHS` clock in PMC), rather than fighting it at the AIC.

One thing worth trying in parallel since `nSRST` clearly isn't giving you a clean UDPHS: does it boot reliably from a **true cold power-cycle with the cable *unplugged*, then plug in after** every time? That's your known-good path and confirms the storm is purely the attached-at-boot race — useful to keep as the working baseline while we nail the permanent fix.

**Found the actual bug.** `AIC_INT_Initialize()` does this:

```c
/* Configure active interrupts */
for(...) { ... AIC_REGS->AIC_IECR = AIC_IECR_Msk; }   // enables source 23 (UDPHS) here
__DSB();
__enable_irq();                                        // ← unmasks CPU IRQs HERE
```

It **enables source 23 in the loop and then calls `__enable_irq()` before returning**. If the UDPHS is asserting (persisted attached+ENDRESET across `nSRST`, host mid-reset), the storm fires the instant `__enable_irq()` runs — *inside* `AIC_INT_Initialize`, before my `SYS_INT_SourceDisable(23)` on the next line ever executes. That's why source 23 is still enabled, `status` is `UNINITIALIZED` (never reached USB init), and why it's a timing-dependent "N loads" race. My mask was structurally too late.

The fix must mask UDPHS **before** that `__enable_irq()`. Let me check the includes then fix it in the right place.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-23 00:58:05Z)**_

Confirmed in the binary: `AIC_INT_Initialize` now selects source 23, writes IDCR (disable), and only *then* `msr CPSR_c` (`__enable_irq`) — the mask is applied **before** IRQs are unmasked, closing the race. Build is clean.

## This is the actual root cause

The whole chain finally makes sense: `AIC_INT_Initialize()` enabled UDPHS (source 23) in its config loop and called `__enable_irq()` **before returning**. With the UDPHS in a persisted attached+ENDRESET state (nSRST doesn't reset it) and a host driving resets, the storm fired the instant `__enable_irq()` executed — inside `AIC_INT_Initialize`, before *any* of my later masks could run. Every fix I placed *after* `AIC_INT_Initialize` was structurally too late, and the tiny timing window is exactly why it took a variable number of loads. Fixing it *inside* `AIC_INT_Initialize`, before `__enable_irq()`, is the only place that wins.

## Test — the previously-failing case

```bash
# cold power-cycle, UDPHS cable attached, FIRST load:
cd firmware/marvin && ./openocd/load-ram.sh
```

This should now boot first-try, every time, cable attached. Please power-cycle and try several times to confirm the determinism (that was the whole failure signature). Then confirm `marvin-perf` still enumerates after boot (validates the sink's deferred `SYS_INT_SourceEnable(UDPHS_IRQn)`).

## Current state of the edits

- **[plib_aic.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/aic/plib_aic.c)** — **THE fix**: UDPHS left masked at the AIC (handler still configured) until the stack is ready.
- **[perf_log_sink_cdc.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c)** — `SYS_INT_SourceEnable(UDPHS_IRQn)` after open+attach. **Required** — it's the other half of the fix.
- **[initialization.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/initialization.c)** — reverted my redundant (race-losing) disable.
- **[drv_usb_udphs_device.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_device.c)** — the ISR no-client detach+mask and the init-detach ordering remain as defensive hardening; not load-bearing for boot now, but both are legitimate independent robustness defects.

If this boots reliably, we've got it. For the Microchip bug report, the headline is now crisp: **`AIC_INT_Initialize` enables all peripheral sources and then unmasks CPU IRQs, so any source whose driver isn't yet initialized (here UDPHS, which can assert ENDRESET from a POR/persisted attached state with a host present) storms the CPU before `SYS_Initialize` can finish** — sources should not be AIC-enabled until their owning driver has a client (or `AIC_INT_Initialize` shouldn't blanket-enable + `__enable_irq` with drivers uninitialized).

Report back on the cold-first-load test and I'll write up the journal entry.

**2026-07-10 — score + streak readers rewritten to integer math; fixed a coverage out-of-bounds bug (pending build).** Converted the shared coverage pipeline (luma → ink threshold → grid resize → per-cell coverage) in `gameplay_score.c` to pure integer so the firmware reproduces the host prototype **bit-for-bit**. This directly cuts hardware misreads: the device was extracting coverage in float32 while templates were built/validated in float64 (plus different rounding modes), so its reads diverged from what was validated. Now luma = `B*29+G*150+R*77` (no /256), ink threshold = rational `GP_{SCORE,STREAK}_INK_NUM/DEN` of the min..max range (`DEN*(luma-lo) ≷ NUM*(hi-lo)`), integer `gp_edge`, integer coverage; no float in the readers (ARM926 has no FPU). **Also fixed a real OOB bug**: when an ink bbox is smaller than the glyph grid, the last cell's block ran past the bbox and read the unused tail of the scratch buffer (stale data) → wrong coverage on short glyphs; clamped `yb→rh`/`xb→rw` to match the host (numpy) slice. Cross-check is now strict bit-exact (presence + every digit + every confidence flag). Digit banks in `gameplay_metadata.h` rebuilt with integer coverage. The old monotonic forward window couldn't represent a value below `last`, so a tens misread locked the value high (11x→14x…); "confident read trumps" fixed that but unmasked a systematic **tens 0↔8 flicker** (the slashed zero's top loop closes under aliasing → reads 8 confidently, 100↔180) and a **carry-roll 900 blip** (mid-roll hundreds reads 9 for ~2 frames at 99→100). Proven host-side (`tools/gameplay`, see its journal 2026-07-10) then ported.
- **Stateless read (`gp_read_streak`, `gameplay_score.c`, pure/cross-checked).** **Presence = the odometer is *locked at its final position*, detected from the note icon — not the digits** (Greg): the counter slides in from the bottom, overshoots, and bounces down to settle (`score-0335.png` = reference locked frame), and mid-slide the cells are misaligned → garbage. The fixed gold note glyph is a position fiducial — its coverage matches the locked template (L1 < `GP_STREAK_NOTE_MAX_SAD`) only when settled, cleanly rejecting both absent and slide/overshoot frames. When locked, three fixed cells (units dark-on-light, tens/hundreds white-on-dark) → 16×10 coverage → integer-L1 argmin over a **per-polarity 0-9 bank**; a wheel failing the gate is flagged unreadable. Fills `{present, digit[3], known[3]}`. Data frozen into `gameplay_metadata.h` (`GP_STREAK_*`: note template + two digit banks + ROIs + thresholds) by `gameplay export-c`. ROIs are absolute (fixed rig; chrome registration exists but is unused in v0).
- **Stateful tracker (`gp_streak_track`/`gp_streak_reset`, state owned by the caller).** **Presence is binary — not present ⇒ streak reset ⇒ 0** (immediate; the sole reset path). While present, **a confident wheel read is authoritative for its place** (Greg: a clear digit read trumps the rollover logic) — it wins even if the value drops, so a misread is a self-correcting one-frame blip; an unreadable (rolling) wheel is filled (holds last, or resets to 0 when a higher place carried). ≥2 confident wheels seed. This replaced a monotonic forward window `[last, last+30]` whose forward-only search couldn't represent a value below `last` → a tens misread locked the value high (11x read as 14x…); confident-trumps fixes it. Host validation over the 6549-frame capture: hand-read anchors exact (100 % in-sample confident-digit accuracy with the refined 8×15 cells), 0 non-reset decreases, correct slide-gating, max 304.

**2026-07-08 — SONG card playtime bar wired; song-info widget rename sync.** An MGS regen renamed the SONG-info section and replaced the hand-built progress-bar hack (`panel_Container_63..66_0` / `panel_Text_15/16_0` / `label__0_00_0` / `label__7_22_0_0`) with three named widgets: `LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_START_TIME` (the "0:00" origin marker), `LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_STOP_TIME`, and a real `leProgressBarWidget` `PROGRESSBAR_DASHBOARD_SONG_PLAYTIME`. The renamed detail labels (Title/Artist/Album/Genre/Tier/Duration/Status) already used stable `LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_*` names, so only the new widgets needed wiring — dashboard code had no references to the removed decorative names.
- **Both time markers are runtime `leFixedString`s** (set up in `song_detail_init` alongside the Status label). `STOP_TIME` tracks the committed selection: `ScreenDashboard_ApplySelection` rewrites it with the song's `m:ss` (same `SongDetail_Duration` string shown in the DURATION field), "-" when unknown. `START_TIME` counts up with elapsed play time (see below); it resets to "0:00" on a fresh selection.
- **Bar fill + elapsed marker = playthrough time.** New feed event `DASH_EVT_PLAYTIME` (`u.play_ms`) + `DashboardFeed_PostPlaytime`. `game_controller.c` `play_until_done` posts `0` at play start (resets bar + marker) and elapsed ms each `GC_PLAY_POLL_MS` (~300 ms) poll. The dashboard consumer calls `ScreenDashboard_ApplyPlaytime`, which clamps elapsed to `s_song_len_s` (captured in ApplySelection), rewrites `START_TIME` as `m:ss` (formatted directly so 0 reads "0:00" — `SongDetail_Duration(0)` gives "-"), and drives the bar at **pixel resolution** via `ProgressBarAA_SetPermille` (0-1000) rather than the stock 0-100 `setValue` (unknown duration → empty bar, un-clamped marker). The 0-100 value quantized the 349px-wide bar to ~3.5px steps — for a long song it held still several seconds then hopped; permille advances it by single pixels.
- **Rounded (pill) bar ends.** New custom widget `ui/widgets/progressbar_aa/` (`ProgressBarAA_EnableRoundImage`) mirrors `panel_aa`: copies the *full progressbar vtable* (so `setValue` etc. survive), overrides `_paint` to run `AaCorners_RenderRoundImage` after the normal draw — eating the four corners back to the card's `SCHEME_PANEL_GRAY_18181B` BASE (resolved at paint time in the active mode). Radius 4 = half the 8px height → full capsule; the fill's leading cap rounds with it (interior pixels preserved). **The radius is carried by the AA pass, not the widget `cornerRadius`:** the stock classic skin's `drawFill` is a plain square `RectFill`, but its `drawBackground` switches to `FillRoundCornerRect` (ArcFills that overshoot the rect — a track visibly taller than the 8px fill) as soon as the widget `cornerRadius` is nonzero. So the widget keeps `cornerRadius` 0 (stock draws a plain square 8px track) and the AA pass owns the rounding. `ScreenDashboard_Setup` also pins the height to 8 (`setSize`, width preserved via `getWidth`). Added to `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake`.
  - **Two-vtable gotcha (why the override first did nothing):** unlike a plain panel (where `panel->fn` *is* the base `widget.fn`), `leProgressBarWidget` holds two pointers to its vtable — its typed `bar->fn` and the base `bar->widget.fn`. The renderer dispatches paint via the *base* `widget.fn->_paint` (it works on a `leWidget*`), so `ProgressBarAA_EnableRoundImage` must repoint **both**; repointing only `bar->fn` leaves the stock paint running and the corners square.
  - **Partial-repaint gotcha (fill-end artifacts):** `AaCorners_RenderRoundImage` re-blends existing pixels toward the backdrop and writes at full-rect coordinates via `_Unsafe` pixel ops (relative to the current frame/damage rect, no bounds check). `panel_aa` is safe because a panel repaints its whole rect. But the stock `setValue` damages only the delta strip between old/new value, so a mid-bar update leaves the frame rect a sliver — the corner writes land outside that tile (garbage) and, over many updates, erode the AA bands into the fill (visible in the first/last ~10%). Fix + smoothness in one: the bar is no longer driven by the stock value at all. `ProgressBarAA_SetPermille` stores a 0-1000 fill fraction and invalidates the *whole* widget; `aa_paint` lets the stock skin draw only the (square) track — the widget value stays 0 so the stock fill is skipped — then draws the fill itself as a `RectFill` of the exact pixel width, then rounds the corners. Full-widget repaint every change keeps the corner writes in-bounds and idempotent, and the pixel-width fill removes the 100-step quantization.
- **Tier string is stars-only** (separate ask): `SongDetail_TierText` drops the " TIER n" suffix — main-setlist songs show just ★×tier, bonus still "BONUS". Shared helper, so song-select dialog and dashboard both change.
- Rides the existing single-consumer/render-lock feed flow — no off-thread widget touch. Files: `ui/screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard.{c,h}`, `ui/dashboard_feed.{c,h}`, `game/game_controller.c`, `ui/widgets/progressbar_aa/*` (new), `ui/song_detail.{c,h}`, `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake`. No MCC/Legato hand-edits (MGS regen staged separately). **Pending Greg's MPLAB build + hardware validation** (stop time matches the selected song; bar fills smoothly over a playthrough and resets on the next run/selection; rounded ends clean with no fill artifacts).

**2026-07-05 — `detect_active` no longer burns CPU while the source is dark.** Follow-on to the `cpu%` work below: VideoTask's active-area detector re-scanned the frame border **every 20 ms tick** while unlatched, and each *failed* scan (dark border) walked the whole band on uncached DDR (~2.6 ms) → ~13% whenever the source was dark (notably: booting while the Wii is asleep). Two fixes, and crucially **it still never gives up** — abandoning detection would permanently mis-frame a source that starts dark and later brightens:
- **Rate-limit:** `detect_active` self-caps to `VIDEO_ACTIVE_SCAN_MS` (100 ms, ~10 Hz) while unlatched instead of every tick. Trade-off: 16-frame accumulation now takes ~1.6 s after the source brightens (was ~0.3 s) — full-frame fallback shows briefly on wake, then snaps to the crop.
- **Dark-gate:** a cheap `frame_has_light()` (coarse grid, stride 64, returns on first bright sample) runs before the heavy border scan; an all-dark frame skips it → ~0 cost. So an asleep/dimmed Wii = near-idle, and detection resumes automatically the instant it brightens. Files: `video/video.c`. Build clean.

Reverted the monitor out of investigation mode: heartbeat cadence 10 s → 60 s; all periodic telemetry (heartbeat line, `SUP:` summary, stack table, startup) → `LOG_DEBUG` (silent at the default INFO level); **`RUNAWAY` stays `LOG_ERROR`** as the always-on watch. The on-card log (`health/heartbeat.csv` + `stacks.txt`) is now behind a compile switch **`HM_SD_LOG_ENABLED` (default 0/off)**; build `-DHM_SD_LOG_ENABLED=1` to restore the crash-timing record (SD-only helpers gated too, so it's warning-clean either way). Re-investigate via `log_set_level(LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG)` and/or the `-D`. Build clean in both switch states. File: `health/health_monitor.c`.
- **Follow-up — `health` now shows a recent-window `cpu%`, not cumulative-since-boot.** The old table used `ulRunTimeCounter / total_since_boot`, a lifetime average with no decay — it buried *current* load under startup (e.g. VideoTask's boot-time active-area scan reading as a steady "13%" long after it had latched). `HealthMonitor_Report` now snapshots, waits `HM_REPORT_WINDOW_MS` (500 ms), snapshots again, and reports each task's share of *that* window (the supervisor's delta math, on demand). `health` takes ~½ s to answer and shows what tasks are doing *now*. 254:| 2026-05-20 | Relax Microchip's host CDC-ACM Communications-interface protocol check to accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0x00 (None)` in addition to `0x01 (AT_V250)` | The fretboard hardware exposes its UART to marvin via the on-board EDBG debugger's CDC ACM (composite VID=0x03EB PID=0x2175: HID + CDC ACM IAD + vendor + MSC). EDBG declares the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol=0x00` rather than the AT-command protocol Microchip hardcodes. The TPL/IAD match accepts the device (host stack does call `interfaceAssign`), but the per-interface check inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` then rejects the comm interface, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to STATE_ERROR, and our attach handler never fires. Both are CDC ACM in practice and Linux/macOS accept either. Two-line OR per check in `usb_host_cdc.c`; logged as patch #7 in the re-apply list. |
255:| 2026-05-20 | `USB_HOST_Initialize` ordering relative to `DRV_USB_EHCI/OHCI_Initialize` and `Legato_Initialize` is **not** load-bearing — keep MCC's emitted order | A prior session hand-edited `initialization.c` to move `USB_HOST_Initialize` *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits on the theory that the host layer needed the HCD interfaces present at init time. Empirical retest with the CDC diagnostic logging in place: MCC's original order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well. The host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time, not at `USB_HOST_Initialize`. Reverted the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. (This is unrelated to patch #6, which is the *peripheral* init order — MMU/AIC ahead of TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC — that one is still a real regression and stays in the list.) |
317:- **`vApplicationMallocFailedHook` AND `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` are silent infinite-loops.** ([freertos_hooks.c](../default/src/config/default/freertos_hooks.c)) Both are MCC defaults: `taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS()` then `for (;;)`. **The malloc hook already bit us (2026-06-25 heap-exhaustion decision):** a `pvPortMalloc` failure during `SYS_Initialize` spun with IRQs off before `log_init`, presenting as a dead board with zero DBGU output — cost a multi-step bisect to find. Patch **both** hooks to emit a marker (even a raw fixed-string DBGU write — heap is full / stack is corrupt, so avoid large stack frames and dynamic work) before the spin; this is an MCC re-apply patch (freertos_hooks.c is generated). An actual overflow/exhaustion is otherwise indistinguishable from any other freeze on hardware. Patch the hook to emit a `LOG_ERR` line naming the offending task before the spin (carefully — the stack is already corrupt, so the hook should avoid using locals or large stack frames). Already nearly bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. (HWM/RUNTIME records reach the host now post-2026-05-29 work, so we have *steady-state* stack visibility — but a real overflow still freezes silently.)
325:- **MCC-file modifications maintenance risk.** A from-scratch MCC regen on 2026-05-15 confirmed **four** local modifications get clobbered. The 2026-05-20 USB-host regen added a fifth. Re-apply after every regen:
357:  8. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. Re-apply after every maXTouch MCC regen.
359:  9. **`gfx/legato/image/png/legato_imagedecoder_png.c` `_render()` — PNG image-to-image decode fix.** Stock `_render` (the path `leImage_Render`/`leImage_Copy`/`leProcessImage` use for PNG) is broken: it (a) ignores `lodepng_decode_memory`'s return, (b) omits the lodepng→Legato channel byte-swap that the working `_draw()` applies (RGBA8888 byte-reverse / `leColorSwap` for RGB888), and (c) `lePixelBufferCopy`s from `src->buffer` (the **compressed** input) instead of a buffer wrapping the decoded pixels → garbage out. Confirmed on hardware: `_draw` is correct, only `_render` is affected (so on-paint `leImageWidget` PNGs work, but pre-decode-to-buffer doesn't). Root cause = the decode was *duplicated* in `_draw`/`_render` and the `_render` copy drifted. Fix = **dedupe**: factor the decode+byte-swap into a shared `_pngDecodeToImage()` helper; `_draw()` then draws the result and `_render()` `lePixelBufferCopy`s it into `dst` — the only legitimate per-path difference. The file is left as a **clean release-style fix** (no in-file re-apply markers, by request) — so this journal entry + `legato_png_render_bug.md` are the record; **watch for silent loss on MCC/MGS regen** until the upstream-fixed gfx ships. **Bug to be filed upstream (Greg/Microchip).** Needed for the album-art pre-cache (`game/art.c`), which decodes PNG covers into RGBA8888 slots via `leImage_Render`.
361:  10. **`gfx/legato/legato_config.h` — `LE_VARIABLEHEAP_SIZE` 524288 → 2097152 (2 MB).** lodepng decodes a full PNG into the Legato variable heap, peaking ~`W*H*(srcBpp+4)` transient (508×208 RGBA ≈ 740 KB), which overflows the default 512 KB → intermittent `LODEPNG_OUT_OF_MEMORY` (err 83) on ~25–30% of the 60 cover decodes (heap fragmentation across the sequential decode/free churn tips some over). 2 MB gives ample margin. Set in MCC (Graphics → Legato memory) if it exposes the knob, else re-apply this literal. Only required while large covers are PNG.
